Name of the Surah

• It is called Al-Buruj (The Mansions of the Stars), because it opens with Allah's oath by the buruj (mansions) in the sky, which are the wandering stars within it.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• An oath concerning the destruction of the criminals who cast the believers into the fire in order to seduce them from their religion. It contains a parable for those who persecuted the Muslims in Makkah, that they are like those (criminals), and a consolation for the believers regarding what befell their predecessors of severe torture, the like of which did not reach them. It also speaks of Allah's power to take vengeance upon His enemies who tormented His servants and His allies, and it presents the parable of the people of Pharaoh and Thamud as a lesson to be considered.

[The Tafsir]

Allah the Exalted swears by the sky with its mansions through which the sun and the moon pass, and by the Day of Resurrection, which Allah promised that He would gather creation on, and by the witness who bears witness, and the witnessed-upon thing that is witnessed against. (Allah, glory be to Him, swears by whatever He wills of His creation, but it is not permissible for a created being to swear by other than Allah, for swearing by other than Allah is shirk.) Cursed were those who dug into the earth a great trench, to torment the believers, and who kindled the fierce fire full of fuel, while they sat beside the trench, staying close to it, and they were present witnessing what they were doing to the believers of punishment and torture. They did not punish them with this severe chastisement except because they believed in Allah, the Almighty who cannot be overcome, the Praiseworthy in His sayings, His actions and His attributes, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And He, glory be to Him, is Witness over all things, nothing is hidden from Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 85, verse 10:

Indeed, those who burned the believing men and believing women with fire, in order to turn them away from the religion of Allah, and then did not repent, for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of Hellfire, and for them is the severe, burning torment.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "The Simplified Tafsir," i.e., explanation of the Qur'an) on Surah 85, verse 11:**

﴿Indeed, those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did righteous deeds will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great attainment.﴾

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 85, verses 12–16:

Indeed, the retribution of your Lord against His enemies and His punishment for them is severe and mighty. Indeed, it is He who originates creation and then restores it, and He is the Forgiving toward whoever repents, abundant in affection and love for His allies, the Lord of the Throne, the Glorious, who has reached the limit in excellence and generosity, the Accomplisher of whatever He wills; nothing He wills can be prevented from Him.

Has the report reached you, O Messenger, of the armies of disbelief that denied their prophets: Pharaoh and Thamud, and what befell them of punishment and retribution? The people did not take heed from that. Rather, those who disbelieve persist in continuous denial, following the same course as those before them. Allah has encompassed them in knowledge and power; nothing of them or of their deeds is hidden from Him. The Qur'an is not as the deniers and polytheists claimed, that it is poetry and sorcery, so they denied it. Rather, it is a glorious, noble Qur'an, in a Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), which no alteration or distortion can reach.
